preamble: Delateralization of the palatalized lateral [lʲ] to the palatal glide [j]: the lateral gesture is lost and the secondary palatal articulation remains as the whole consonant. This is documented in the Carpatho-Rusyn dialect of Komlóska (Komloška), north-eastern Hungary, where palatalized ľ became j in all positions. In Old East Slavic, l was palatalized before front vowels, as in хлѣбъ /ˈxlʲeːbʊ/ 'bread' and желѣзо /ʑɛˈlʲeːzɔ/ 'iron', which appear in Komlóska as chjib and zejizo.

examples.note: Palatalized lateral after a consonant > j (Ukrainian хліб keeps the lateral).

sources: Benedek, G. (2007). Судьба палатализованного л' в русинском говоре села Комлошка [The fate of palatalized l' in the Rusyn dialect of Komlóska]. Studia Slavica, 52(1–2), 39–42. https://doi.org/10.1556/SSlav.52.2007.1-2.6
